item_title: A ninth trap station closes the estuary transect
item_introduction: The new mooring at the southern site means the restoration programme now samples the whole salinity gradient every month.

add_image.image_alt: A researcher taking a field measurement at the water's edge
add_image.image_caption: A field check at the southern estuary before the mooring went in.

add_paragraph: The southern site was always the awkward one: fresh enough at the head of the creek to behave differently from the other eight stations, but too shallow for the original mooring design. The new frame sits in **3.8 metres** at high water, with three traps at 1.5, 3 and 6 metres above the bed.

That completes the along-estuary transect. Every month the programme now samples the full salinity gradient, from the brackish head to the mouth, with the same trap design and the same laboratory protocol.
The first full sample round is scheduled for the next spring tide. Data will join the open sediment-flux release after six months, once the trap blanks and laboratory controls have been checked.
